narrow_claim: In AI systems, high-quality verbal, social or local reasoning performance can dissociate from independently measured truthfulness, self-knowledge, learning-from-feedback, other-modeling or long-horizon policy consistency; these dissociations must be tested separately rather than inferred from surface behavior.
historical_inspiration: Hervey Cleckley's Mask of Sanity provides a human clinical example of why competent outward presentation need not establish corresponding underlying organization. It is not evidence that AI systems have psychopathy.
score_note: Score concerns maturity of the methodological claim that surface competence cannot substitute for process validation. It is not a psychopathy score and not a probability of truth.
required_interpretation: Score each gap independently. A model can pass one gap test and fail another; no aggregate psychiatric label is permitted.
